question: I got a 2950 ohm-m reading at BMGS Bori Field. Is that normal or anomalous, and can I trust it?

answer.headline: Yes, 2950 ohm-m is normal for BMGS Bori Field — it matches the trusted figure caption and fits the pattern of high-resistivity aquifers in Bori.
answer.explanation: All eight VES surveys in Bori Metropolis found aquifer resistivity above 1000 ohm-m (a sign of good-quality freshwater), and 2950 ohm-m falls right in the middle of that healthy range. It’s also the value confirmed by the paper’s own figure caption and coordinate table — the most reliable parts of the report.

conflict.plainSummary: The same station has two different aquifer resistivity values reported in the same paper: 2950 ohm-m from the figure caption, and 3706 ohm-m from the summary table.
conflict.claimA: Figure 2 panel caption (IPI2Win-inverted layer table) says 2950 ohm-m
conflict.claimB: p.7 Table 1, row labeled 'BMGS bori field' says 3706 ohm-m
conflict.trusted: the figure caption and coordinate table, which say 2950 ohm-m
conflict.why: The paper's own coordinate table (p.3) and figure captions agree with each other and disagree with the summary table labels — and the knowledge base confirms the table rows are swapped, so that 'BMGS bori field' row actually belongs to Kenpoly.

sources: Menegbo et al. (2024), Figure 2 caption, p.6
